q1: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2: SELECT DISTINCT P1.EMAIL FROM PERSON P1, PERSON P2 WHERE P1.EMAIL = P2.EMAIL AND P1.ID != P2.ID
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT P1.EMAIL FROM PERSON P1, PERSON P2 WHERE P1.EMAIL = P2.EMAIL AND P1.ID != P2.ID
counterexample: INSERT INTO PERSON (ID, EMAIL) VALUES (1, 'test@example.com'); INSERT INTO PERSON (ID, EMAIL) VALUES (2, 'test@example.com');
explanation: Q1 groups the records by the EMAIL column and filters out the emails that appear more than once. Q2, on the other hand, finds distinct pairs of records with the same email but different IDs.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have at least two records with the same email but different IDs to trigger the difference between the two queries.
